transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Time: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Gomez (Cobalt Head of ML), Ethan Wright (Cobalt Dir. Product), Lia Chen (Cobalt Eng Manager)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Weekly POC sync focused on a regression spike in last night's scoring run.
- Identified ~12 prompts with drop in top-1 accuracy; likely caused by prompt formatting change + model tokenization edge-case.
- Action: Redwood to share per-prompt traces and KV cache snapshots; customer to prioritize top 5 prompts; schedule SE deep dive for batching/latency.

[00:00] Alex: hey team, thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight 45 ish minutes. Quick roll-call?
[00:12] Maya: Maya here, thanks. We saw a fairly surprising regression in the nightly eval, so want to walk through that.
[00:22] Ethan: Ethan here, product — mostly to understand impact on shopping assistant flows.
[00:28] Lia: Lia, eng manager, I'll keep notes on infra ask.
[00:33] Samir: Samir, Redwood SE — I pulled the eval artifacts and a first-pass diff.

[02:10] Alex: quick context — last night we ran the 10k test set, scoring pipeline bumped top-1 accuracy down for a 12 prompt subset, precision drop around 8-12%. Not catastrophic but visible on the dashboard.
[02:32] Maya: we saw similar; conversion rate on sample set down. Question: did you change model version or any tokenization?
[02:41] Samir: no model version swap in the Hosted channel — same v1.3.4 variant. There was a small prompt normalization tweak the customer applied last week — removes trailing punctuation in product titles. That could be the root.
[03:05] Ethan: can you explain how that would cause the score to dip? I thought the model is robust to punctuation.
[03:14] Samir: generally yes, but these prompts rely on structured cues — e.g., SKU: 00123. Removing colon or trailing comma changes token boundaries; with quantized weights small shifts can flip beam preference. Also we saw some guardrail hits that increased false positives.

[04:50] Lia: small note — our dev changed the preprocessor to strip special characters to normalize search queries. Perhaps that broke a few templated prompt templates.
[05:10] Maya: okay, so hypothesis: preproc change + prompt-edge tokenization -> scoring regression. What data do you need from us to confirm?
[05:22] Samir: ideally: exact raw prompt examples for the 12 failures, the post-normalized input, and the expected label. Redwood will provide per-prompt logits and the KV cache snapshot so we can see whether attention patterns differ.

[07:00] Alex: we'll attach the scoring sheet and a short README; note that Redwood can run a delta evaluation with K=1 and K=5 to test mode sensitivity.
[07:15] Maya: good. On the guardrails, we also saw a bump in 'policy flag' hits — they're mostly false positives for product content. How tunable is that threshold?
[07:30] Samir: the guardrail is rule + model hybrid. We can tune score thresholds; there is a little jitter when prompts are short. We recommend adjusting threshold per intent bucket — we can propose thresholds for the shopping assistant vs. returns flow.

[09:00] Ethan: what's the expected impact on latency if we change thresholds or batch sizes? We can't blow up response times.
[09:10] Samir: threshold tuning doesn't affect latency. Batch size changes do; currently pilot is set to batch-size 8 with continuous batching. Increasing to 16 improves throughput but risks tail latency. We can run an experiment during low traffic window.

[10:45] Maya: can Redwood reproduce the regression locally with the inputs we provide?
[10:52] Samir: yes — if you share raw+normalized pairs we can replay in our test harness. We'll also provide per-step logits, tokenization diffs, and a KV cache diff. Note: sometimes the transcript shows K-V cash in the log, our ASR wrote "K V cash" before; ignore that.

[12:30] Lia: any thought it's a model drift issue? We haven't changed weights but maybe the thermal scaling on Dedicated hardware caused quantization noise?
[12:42] Samir: unlikely in Hosted. If on Dedicated, we check kernel selection and quantization profile. For Hosted, rollback isn't needed.

[14:00] Alex: let's walk through three concrete failing examples. Samir, can you screen-share? (screen-share noise)
[14:28] Samir: example one: prompt id 7A12 — user query "What's the dimension of T-45?" Preproc removed dash -> tokenized differently; top prediction shifted from 'Dimension: 12x8' to 'Unknown'.
[15:05] Maya: that's pretty bad — that prompt is high priority.

[17:00] Alex: high-level plan: reproduce failures, generate per-prompt debug artifacts, adjust preproc or prompt template, then re-evaluate. If needed, propose guardrail threshold change for that intent.
[17:22] Ethan: for scope — what's effort estimation for those three steps?
[17:30] Alex: Redwood SE time ~4-8 hours initial analysis; another 2-4 hours for tuning and a short A/B; we can pack that into current pilot SOW unless it balloons.

[19:00] Maya: also want to look at scoring function — currently we pass through model logits into a simple threshold; any ways to smooth?
[19:12] Samir: yes — two low-effort handles: 1) softening threshold with small margin; 2) add a rescoring pass with a dedicated reranker on top of top-k. Both cost tokens but reduce regressions.

[21:10] Lia: token cost implication? We need to watch pilot credits.
[21:18] Alex: provide cost delta estimate — Samir will model token cost and latency for the reranker. We'll include in the spreadsheet.

[23:00] Maya: I'm also worried about false positive guardrail hits stopping flows. Do you have a 'warn-not-block' mode?
[23:10] Samir: yes — we can set policy action to 'warn' and log; then only escalate to 'block' if repeated in a session. That's easy to flip in config.

[25:30] Alex: do we want to add a short regression test per deploy? Maybe a nightly 2k prompt smoke test focused on the 120 critical prompts?
[25:45] Maya: yes, we want that. We'll work with Redwood to pick the set.

[27:00] Ethan: re: artifacts — please put the scoring diff and the example failures into the shared drive.
[27:12] Alex: I'll upload the scoring sheet and README to the pilot folder: https://redwood.app/pilot/cobalt/scorecard (placeholder).

[29:00] Samir: quick note on quantization: we observed tiny preference changes in low-prob tail tokens when running 4-bit quantization. If you see inconsistent outputs, we can run the same prompts with fp16 to rule that out.
[29:22] Lia: are you running 4-bit in Hosted?
[29:28] Samir: Hosted uses mixed profiles, model variant in pilot was using q4_0; we can run a fp16 comparison.

[31:05] Maya: what's the timeline you mentioned for per-prompt traces?
[31:10] Samir: we can turn around per-prompt debug by EOD Friday (2025-11-07) if we get the raw prompts today.

[33:00] Alex: any blockers on Cobalt side to share prompts?
[33:12] Maya: we'll share top 50 raw + normalized by tomorrow morning. Ethan will confirm the business-critical top 5.

[35:00] Ethan: second ask — can Redwood run a quick latency/batching matrix? e.g., batch sizes [8,16,32], p95.
[35:12] Samir: yes — needs a short slot; propose SE deep dive next week to run controlled experiments.

[36:30] Lia: while we're here, minor backlog item — SSO metadata update for our pilot account. I opened a ticket.
[36:40] Alex: noted, we'll follow up in separate thread.

[38:00] Maya: one more question: on the reranker idea, do you maintain separate dev config for each intent? How heavy is per-intent tuning?
[38:14] Samir: we recommend per-intent thresholds and a light-weight reranker per high-value intent. Setting up is a couple of hours per intent plus tuning.

[40:00] Alex: OK let's recap and assign owners. Samir will produce traces and KV cache snapshot for 12 fails (due 11/07). Maya/Ethan to prioritize top 5 and share raw/normalized pairs (due 11/06). Alex to send updated pilot billing + scoring sheet (due 11/09). Schedule SE deep dive for week of 11/10.

[42:00] Maya: thanks — this feels actionable.
[42:12] Ethan: agree. Quick ask — can you also include per-prompt tokenization diffs in the sheet?
[42:20] Samir: yes will include tokenization column and top-k logits.

[44:00] Alex: any other business?
[44:05] Lia: none from infra.
[44:08] Maya: no.
[44:15] Alex: great we'll close there. Follow-ups in the shared pilot folder. Thanks everyone.
[44:30] (meeting ends)
